question: What protections from fear and bodily harm are granted to the human practitioner?
premises: Fear is negated for the man.
Falling or destruction of the body is negated.
inference: The practitioner has no fear, no loss of speech, and no falling of the body.
uncertainties: The exact sense of vāk in relation to kāya-pātanam is somewhat compressed.
plain_english: There is no fear for the man, nor loss of speech, nor falling of the body.
